page.overview:
Who is God?

God is, according to the Abrahamic religions, creator and ruler as well as the sustainer of the Universe.

"God" is used in interjections by William Dyer, (: At the Mountains of Madness) Marinus Bicknell Willett, (: The Case of Charles Dexter Ward), Henry Armitage and Francis Morgan, (: The Dunwich Horror) the reanimated Eric Moreland Clapham-Lee, (: Herbert West--Reanimator) Zadok Allen, (: The Shadow Over Innsmouth) Henry Wentworth Akeley, the Speech-Machine and Albert Wilmarth, (: The Whisperer in Darkness) Francis Wayland Thurston, (: "The Call of Cthulhu") a Boston surveyor and Ammi Pierce, (: "The Colour Out of Space") an addicted narrator, (: "Dagon") Robert Blake, (: "The Haunter of the Dark") a poet narrator, (: "He") a grave-robbing narrator,(: "The Hound") Davis and a doctor colleague, (: "In the Vault") a monster-hunter narrator , (: "The Lurking Fear") Sheehan, (: "Old Bugs") the outsider, (: "The Outsider"), Richard Upton Pickman and a narrator, (: "Pickman's Model") Delapore and the oldest man of his party, (: "The Rats in the Walls") Harley Warren, (: "The Statement of Randolph Carter") Edward Derby and Daniel Upton, (: "The Thing on the Doorstep") Jervas Dudley, (: "The Tomb") a migrant narrator, (: "The Transition of Juan Romero") Carter, (: "The Unnamable") Lovecraft, (: "The Very Old Folk") Powers Meredith, (: "Bothon") Dr McNeill and a Native American ethnologist narrator, (: "The Curse of Yig") Alonzo Typer, (: "The Diary of Alonzo Typer") a resurrected leper narrator (: "The Disinterment")

Obed Marsh mocked Innsmouth inhabitants for praying to him. (: The Shadow Over Innsmouth)

A de la Poer was allegedly 'cursed of God', (: "The Rats in the Walls") and "An Act of God" is a legal term. (: "Bothon")
